The Gerontissa Icon of the Theotokos

Icons

Theotokos

The Gerontissa Icon of the Theotokos

Eldress · Gerondissa

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Gerontissa is Pantokrator Monastery’s principal revered Marian image. The monastery explains its name through the tradition of a dying elder who wished to receive Communion.

[1] Principal icon and name

What is depicted

The displayed Gerontissa shows the Mother of God standing alone, without Christ in her arms. Her body and hands turn to one side. A metal revetment covers much of the figure; the face and the long vertical form remain visible. This is a specific full-length composition, not a seated Mother-and-Child panel.

[2] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

History and tradition

The monastery places the icon’s history near its fourteenth-century foundation but distinguishes that history from the painted appearance, which it dates to the nineteenth century. It relates a period in a well during pirate raids. Its location moved from behind the altar into the main church after the event associated with the elder.

[1] Principal history and iconography

Published explanation

In the received account, the celebrant delays while the elder is near death; the Mother of God’s voice from the icon urges him to act. The elder receives Communion and reposes. The monastery explicitly treats this as Athonite tradition.

[1] Name-giving event

An 1869 coloured engraving by Ioannis Kaldis records the standing composition with miniature scenes of the monastery, the finding in the well and the filling of empty oil jars. That dated print provides a separate historical witness to the nineteenth-century imagery.
